DAMARIS LADY MASHAM AN LEIBNIZ

Date: Oates, 29. März (9. April) 1704. [56.67.]
Series: Band II 4 (1701 - 1707)
Number: 63.
Sequence: 63

[[204.15]] 63. DAMARIS LADY MASHAM AN LEIBNIZ

[[204.16]] Oates, 29. März (9. April) 1704. [56.67.]

[[205.9]] S^#'r Oates 29 March 1704

[[205.10]] Thō I am not in the Number of those who can confirm the advantageous Idea you have of

[[205.11]] English Ladys yet I have been too much conversant amongst Learned Men not to have

[[205.12]] contracted (so far as I am capable of it) a Just Value for them or to have been ignorant of the

[[205.13]] rank you hold in the Commonwealth of Letters. This has dispos'd me long since to entertain

[[205.14]] with Pleasure any Occasion of testifying a great Respect for you; and has lately suggested to me

[[205.15]] that my Fathers Intellectual System might, possibly, not be unacceptable to you. The

[[205.16]] esteem you express for that Work pleases me very much both on this account, and also as it is a

[[205.17]] new Confirmation to me of the Worth of that Performance.

[[205.18]] I should be glad to have a farther view into the Intellectual World; and would therefore

[[205.19]] willingly have right Conceptions of the System you propose. To this Purpose upon the receit of

[[205.20]] your obliging Letter, I look'd into the Article of Rorarius in the first Edition of M^#'r Bayls

[[205.21]] Dictionarie (not haveing the 2^#'d by me) and being by his quotation of you there, directed to the

[[205.22]] Journal des Savans 1695 I read what is there publish'd of it.

[[205.23]] Perhaps my not being accustom'd to such abstract Speculations made me not well

[[205.24]] comprehend what you say there of Formes, upon which I think you build your Hypothesis: for

[[205.25]] (as it seemes to me) you sometimes call them Forces Primitives, sometimes des Ames

[[205.26]] sometimes Formes constitutives des substances, and sometimes Substances themselves;

[[205.27]] but such yet as are neither Spirit, nor matter whence I confess I have no cleare Idea of what

[[205.28]] you call Formes.

[[205.29]] That a man whose Correspondence is so highly esteem'd as yours by all the Learned men

[[205.30]] of Europe should employ any of his valuable Moments in the instruction of an Ignorant Woman

[[205.31]] is what I should not perhaps presume to importune you for, if your character was known to me

[[206.1]] onely as a Learned Man; for those who are far advanced in Learned Studies, and high

[[206.2]] Speculations may think themselves excus'd from such a Condescention; but you I am confident

[[206.3]] would not contemne the most Ignorant Lover of Truth; were I not secur'd by my sex of a

[[206.4]] favorable distinction from the obligeing Civilitie of a Man Conversant in Courts.

[[206.5]] I take the libertie therefore to request the favour of you that you will by some explication

[[206.6]] or definition of them help me to Conceive what your Formes are; for I cannot but desire to

[[206.7]] understand a Systeme recommended to me not onely by the eminence of its Author, but

[[206.8]] particularly also as tending to inlarge our Idea of the Divine Perfections, and the Beautie of his

[[206.9]] Works. If you please to add in short the Sum of your Answers to M^#'r Bayles objections in his

[[206.10]] second edition of his Dictionarie it will be an Additional Obligation in giveing me still further

[[206.11]] Light into this matter.

[[206.12]] I have order'd my Fathers Discourse concerning the Lords Supper to be sent you together

[[206.13]] with his Intellectual System in the same vol: the Value you express for the Author makes me

[[206.14]] think you will not dislike to look into anything of his and thō this Treatise was writ when he

[[206.15]] was a Young Man, yet it was Highly commended by our Famous Selden.

[[206.16]] You will much oblige me in accepting of this Book as from one who is with great Esteem

[[206.17]] and Respect

[[206.18]] S^#'r Your very Humble Servant Da Masham.

[[206.19]] M^#'r Locke (whose company I am so Happy as to injoy in my Familie) desires me to present

[[206.20]] you his Humble Service.
